A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUIT research. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are available and sufficiently readable to match content across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v2 reports original knowledge-editing experiments on CounterFact and zsRE, alongside capability evaluations, ablations, and subspace analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds batch-size comparisons and cross-model hyperparameter sweeps, including results in Table 1 and Appendix C.3.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same SVD-based key projection, two-direction residual update, directional penalty, and AlphaEdit weight-update formula. Terminology changes and different selected hyperparameters do not introduce a new algorithm or component.

E1.justification: Both use PARAREL, CounterFact, zsRE, MMLU/GLUE, CHED, RippleEdits, and Wikinews material. The larger-model and 5,000-edit evaluations already appear in v2's appendices. Added batch sizes and model-specific sweeps change experimental settings within retained task coverage.

E2.justification: The overall baseline roster is retained. However, v3 Table 2 adds FT-L, MEND, MEMIT, and PMET to the strict original-response zsRE preservation comparison, which v2 Table 7 reports only for AlphaEdit and SUIT. Adding an AlphaEdit row to the ablation table redisplays a comparison already made in v2's prose.

E3.justification: v3 adds CounterFact batch sizes 1 and 10 while retaining 1,000 total edits. Its main zsRE evaluation replaces batch-local preservation with the original-response, end-of-sequence test already present in v2 Appendix E.2.2. SUIT's stated energy threshold changes from 0.4 for all models to 0.6 for GPT-J and Qwen2.5, and the hyperparameter sweep excludes zero. These materially revise the reported evaluation settings without establishing that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a substantial robustness analysis of frequent cumulative updates through smaller batch sizes, exposing baseline collapse while testing SUIT's stability. Appendix C.3 adds energy-threshold sensitivity sweeps for GPT-J and Qwen2.5, and Figure 5 is revised. The gold-answer specificity diagnostic in v2 Table 6 is removed; v3 instead reports filtering yield. Existing CHED, ripple, component, sample-size, and heatmap analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Averaging over examples and measuring representation variance remain unchanged practices, rather than newly introduced uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive batch-size and hyperparameter-sweep results and expands strict zsRE results. GPT-J SUIT's batch-100 CounterFact S changes from 82.3 to 84.7 alongside the changed energy threshold, so this is not an established same-setting gain. Figure 5 also changes, and Tables 8–9 add harmonic-mean scores. CHED averages are corrected from 74.2 to 74.5 for MEMIT and 93.4 to 93.7 for SUIT. Some updated main-table scores remain unreconciled with older values retained in Appendix Table 8.

T1.justification: The AlphaEdit update mathematics, SVD subspace construction, and orthogonal magnitude-swap derivation are retained across the reorganized appendices. Renamed variables and the explicit standard exact-match formula do not introduce new theory; the strict preservation criterion already existed in v2.

C1.justification: Both versions present SUIT as restricting key and residual computations to edit-relevant subspaces to improve knowledge preservation while maintaining effective editing and general capabilities. The rewritten abstract and conclusion emphasize the same contribution; the additional experiments support retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 uses similar spectral curves to justify a shared energy threshold. v3 removes that inference, explains model-dependent sensitivity, and notes that excessive removal can eliminate directions needed for editing. It also interprets small-batch failures through cumulative weight updates and clarifies why context interventions must precede the entity in a causal language model.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the promised future code-and-data release with stated code availability and a repository link. Appendix C.2 clarifies zero-based layer indexing and documents the sweep grid and model-specific selected thresholds. Hardware and precomputation-cost information were already provided in v2.

R1.justification: v3 adds Mitchell et al.'s Memory-based Model Editing at Scale and expands discussion of the tradeoffs among editing paradigms. It more explicitly positions SUIT's key/value constraints relative to AlphaEdit's weight-update constraint. Consolidated MMLU and GLUE references concern works already cited.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, evaluation narrative, hyperparameter discussion, and entity/context appendix undergo substantial rewriting. v3 adds an organized additional-experiments subsection, merges the regularization appendix into Appendix A, and replaces subject/object terminology with entity/attribute throughout.

P2.justification: The combined main benchmark table becomes separate CounterFact and zsRE tables with nested batch-size and token-length columns. v3 adds a sweep table, expands Tables 8–9 with S columns, and redraws Figure 5 with revised axes and styling. Numerous tables and captions are reformatted or relocated; the other plotted evidence and appendix heatmaps are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens evaluation through frequent-update stress tests, broader strict zsRE comparisons, and direct evidence for model-specific tuning. Clearer exposition, corrected CHED averages, and stated code access also help. The gain is limited because much supplementary evidence already existed, and Table 8 retains older GPT-J and Qwen2.5 SUIT scores without clearly reconciling them with the updated main results.
